**Finding: compliant (at fallback) — no redline.**

Section 13, read together with the continuation at p0090–p0093, does contain a genuine vendor-side IP indemnity, despite the heading paragraph (p0087) itself only reciting Garman's ownership:

- **Vendor indemnity present:** Garman warrants it owns/controls all necessary rights with no encumbrances, and agrees to indemnify and hold Sparkling harmless for all Losses (court costs, settlement amounts, reasonable legal fees, investigation costs) from breach of that warranty.
- **Standard remedy ladder:** procure the right, procure an equivalent element, or replace/modify so the Work is non-infringing without material loss of functionality.
- **No reverse indemnity:** nothing in the document imposes a Sparkling indemnity for Garman's software or services, so the walk-away case is absent.
- **Better than fallback on cap:** Section 15 states the limitation of liability "shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14" — so the IP indemnity is uncapped and outside the consequential-damages exclusion, exceeding the fallback's 3× super-cap.

Sub-elements short of preferred, noted rather than flagged: no express "defend"/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund fallback remedy, indemnity limited to IP/title (no breach-of-law, data-breach or gross-negligence limbs), affiliates unnamed, and a tight ten-calendar-day notice obligation. These are worth raising in negotiation but do not fail the fallback.
